enumeration_note: The video teaches one runnable skeleton â€” fading liquidity-sweep rejections at untapped HTF support/resistance on the 5m/1m for a 1:2 scalp. The 'trap' fade is the confirmation mechanic of that same setup, and the twice-rejection double bottom is a compatible variant (same entry/exit skeleton, same 1:2 target); enumerated as one strategy with two variants.

coaching_notes: Find where the obvious trades are sitting, and do the opposite.
Look for clean price action that's just a little too clean â€” equal highs, trend lines, perfect zones â€” that's the bait.
Avoid entering before the price taps the liquidity zone. Wait for confirmation.
Do not chase the breakouts. Wait for price to trap traders and fade the move.
Anticipate where price is going, not react to it.
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: mark higher-time-frame (daily/4H) swing highs/lows and clean support/resistance levels first, using the horizontal line tool
SELECTION: only target untapped HTF levels (liquidity lives where price hasn't tapped yet)
ENTRY GATE: wait for price to actually tap the marked liquidity zone before entering (do not enter pre-tap)
ENTRY TRIGGER: rapid price approach to the level + volume spike + quick tap + rejection wick
ENTRY CONFIRMATION: exhaustion candle / long wick / bullish or bearish engulfing / volume divergence
TRAP CONFIRMATION: wick above resistance then dump, or wick below support then reverse â€” fade the fake break
DIRECTION: long on swept support rejection, short on swept resistance rejection
STOP: below the sweep low (e.g. below current London low) / beyond the marked S/R level; for double bottom the bar must not close below the level
VARIANT SUB-MECHANIC: double bottom = second rejection of the same area with no close below the level â†’ full reversal trade at 1:2
SESSION FILTER: trade around London or New York open (when the most stop hunts occur)
strategies.entry_summary: Mark untapped higher-time-frame (daily/4H) support/resistance liquidity zones, then drop to the 5-minute (or 1-minute) chart and wait for price to rapidly approach and tap a marked level with a volume spike. Enter the reversal (fade the sweep) on a rejection wick confirmed by an exhaustion candle, long wick, bullish/bearish engulfing, or volume divergence. Long at swept support, short at swept resistance.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop loss below the sweep low (e.g. below the current London low) / beyond the marked S/R level; target a fixed 1:2 risk-to-reward.
strategies.name: ltf_liquidity_sweep_rejection_scalp

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: single tap of the level + rejection wick + volume spike + engulfing/exhaustion candle
variants.target_note: 1:2 risk-to-reward, stop below London low / below the level
variants.timeframe_note: 5-minute (or 1-minute if riskier) entry off daily/4H marked levels
variants.transcript_quote: you are simply waiting for one of these levels to be hit and then you're looking for that rejection wick... you can get into your scalping trade and get a 1 to2 risk-to-reward setup

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: price rejects the same area twice with the bar not closing below the S/R level (double bottom full reversal)
variants.transcript_quote: if price rejects the same area twice, it could be a full reversal double bottom with the bar not closing below the area of support and resistance that you marked up and getting another trade 1:2 risk-to-reward ratio
